Subject: Production tail latency causing timeouts - urgent

Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency for our nightly batch between 02:10-02:25 UTC this morning. Topline: p99 -> 1.2s (normally ~120ms), p99.9 spikes to 3.5s, and several job shards timed out which produced 429/502s downstream. Throughput dropped ~30% during the window. This is impacting our billing reconciliation job and will block the morning ingest if it reoccurs.

From: rachel_kim@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, Jared Holt <jared.holt@acme-corp.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-10T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Production tail latency causing timeouts - urgent

Adding a quick technical readout from the runtime team. Initial hypotheses and what we need to verify:

1) Queueing/backpressure at the front of the serving runtime: we’ve seen long-tail latency when a burst of concurrent short requests floods request queues and induces per-instance queuing that is not visible at aggregate QPS. This looks like classic head-of-line queueing.

2) KV cache churn: if the workload has variable prefixes or very different prompt lengths, the KV cache hit-rate can drop and cause a cascade of slower token generation for some requests.

3) Concurrency caps & slot starvation: our current per-instance concurrency default for hosted routes is 64 active requests. If a handful of customer sessions occupy many slots (large sequences, long TTIs), they can starve short requests.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (we can enact immediately):
- Temporarily increase route concurrency cap to 128 for acme-prod routes for the next 60–90 min (monitor closely).
- Apply a lightweight smoothing rate limit at the edge (burst=100, sustained=30rps) to avoid large instantaneous bursts.
- Enable prefix/KV warm caching for the batch job route where possible.
- Collect full spans for the 02:10–02:25 window + runtime instance logs (we can provide commands).

What I’m attaching: a short config diff we can apply to the routing layer and a note on how to collect traces. Please confirm you’ve uploaded the full traces file.

Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: config_diff.patch)

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-04-10T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production tail latency causing timeouts - urgent

Action log from Eng/SRE:

- 09:10 UTC: Increased acme-prod route concurrency cap from 64 -> 128 and routed 20% of traffic to a dedicated pool (canary).
- 09:18 UTC: Enabled edge smoothing policy for acme-prod (burst=120, sustained=40rps).
- 09:32 UTC: Rolled a targeted restart of three serving instances suspected of cache thrash (no rolling outage expected).

Preliminary telemetry: timeouts dropped ~75% within first 10 minutes and throughput recovered to ~90% of baseline; long-tail p99.9 reduced but still present at 1.1s for some request patterns.

Next steps:
- We’ll pull full span details and correlate with per-instance queue lengths. Look for requests that show large queue wait time vs compute time.
- If KV miss-rate is confirmed, we’ll enable prefix caching and consider increasing KV cache size for that pool.

If the customer still sees residual spikes after our short-term actions, we should escalate to an exec briefing and propose a reserved capacity window while we rollout a config change. I’ll be on the 3pm call.

-Vivek
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime

Thanks — the temporary cap increase and smoothing helped a lot; we saw a marked reduction in 502s/timeouts for the immediate batch window. That said, we still observed intermittent long-tail spikes around 02:18 and 02:22 UTC that caused a few shard retries. I’ve uploaded the full exported traces to the Drive link and included raw client logs showing a burst of 360 concurrent short requests from our side (cron fanout).

I don’t love the idea of sustained higher concurrency caps as a long-term fix — if this is queueing we’d prefer a deterministic mitigation (reserved capacity or scheduled worker window). Happy to be on the 3pm call to align.

Jared
